name: dsh-superagent
cost: Free (MIT). Model usage costs are not stated in the README
works_with: DeepSeek Harness, GitHub, and optionally Feishu
short: DeepSeek's research prototype of a coding agent that watches one GitHub repo, takes requests and answers with pull requests.
what: It is a bundle for DeepSeek Harness that listens to GitHub and, if you want, Feishu. When an allowed person asks it for work, it opens a work item, does the job in its own session and folder, and replies in the same thread, for example with a pull request. A web panel shows what needs a person. The team's idea is that it acts only when asked or when a rule you wrote allows it.
who: Teams who want to try a proactive agent on a real repo and are comfortable running and debugging research code. DeepSeek calls it a reference prototype, not a product, so skip it if you want something stable.
needs: Node.js 22.19+ or 24+, pnpm, git 2.32+, Python 3.8+ and tmux
A repository on github.com (GitHub Enterprise Server is not supported) and a local clone of it
A separate GitHub user account for the agent, with write access to the repo
A model provider configured for DeepSeek Harness
Optional: `lark-cli` and a Feishu or Lark bot app for chat requests

steps.title: Or let your agent walk you through it
steps.text: The README says setup has many steps, so it suggests asking your coding agent to do it with you. It asks one question at a time and shows the full plan before installing.
steps.code: Read SETUP.md in this repository and set up dsh-superagent with me.

steps.title: Give the agent account its own GitHub CLI
steps.text: For a manual setup, sign in as the agent account. The last command prints its login.
steps.code:
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin
cat > ~/.local/bin/gh-agent <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
GH_CONFIG_DIR="$HOME/.config/gh-agent" exec gh "$@"
EOF
chmod +x ~/.local/bin/gh-agent
gh-agent auth login
gh-agent api user --jq .login

steps.title: Install the harness and the bundle
steps.text: Run this once, on a machine with no `superagent` profile yet. Replace `<this repository>` with the repo's address.
steps.code:
npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.3
git clone <this repository> dsh-superagent && cd dsh-superagent
pnpm install && pnpm build
dsh superagent --from-default-profile web --dump-config > /dev/null
dsh plugin --profile superagent add "link:$PWD"

steps.title: Add the machine settings
steps.text: Copy `examples/profile.cordis.patch.yml` to `~/.dsh/profiles/superagent/cordis.patch.yml` and fill in every `<placeholder>`. `stateDir` must be an absolute path.

steps.title: Start it
steps.text: `start` runs it in a tmux session and prints any missing setup. Open the URL in the log and choose Superagent in the sidebar.

steps.title: Finish setup in the panel
steps.text: Under Sources, set the repo (`owner/name`) and the path to `gh-agent`. Under Policy, add the GitHub accounts allowed to ask for work. Until that list has someone in it, no request becomes a ticket. Under Execution, set the work folder and a prepare command.

try.label: From the README
try.text: From an allowed account, open a new issue or comment that mentions the agent account. It picks it up on the next poll. Editing an old issue to add a mention does not count, so post a new comment.

watch: DeepSeek says this is research code for reference, not an official product. It may have bugs, and some ideas in their article are not built yet.

Both agent presets run with `danger-full-access` as your OS user. A worker can run programs and read your home folder. For isolation, the docs suggest a separate OS account that holds only the agent's credentials.
The agent comments, pushes branches and opens pull requests as its own GitHub account. A GitHub App cannot be used.
The plugin changes process-wide `PATH` and git settings, so keep the `superagent` profile separate from the one you work in.
Running the profile creation command again on an existing install replaces the profile and deletes its machine settings. Do not use it to upgrade.
